title: The Educated Barbarian: Hagakure analysis (part. 8)
summary: NH continues the Hagakure commentary: devotion to one path, the danger of theory without practice and armchair experts, accepting hardship like a downpour, immersion through daily practice, and guarding against manipulation. He links each to lifting and his own training habits.
claims: A big following reflects followers' intellect and the leader's marketing more than the leader's worth
To be truly good at something put most effort into one path; other pursuits should feed it
Intellectuals who live only in theory stop growing, inflate their egos and split hairs; you need a balance of physical and mental
Armchair experts argue about fitness they don't practice to feel superior; he doesn't bother debating them
Some people build circular arguments so they are never wrong; talking with them is pointless
If you accept hardship from the start it stops being hardship; that's why training is doable and even enjoyable
Lifters with a martyr attitude toward training don't stick with it
You eventually must pick one path and stop switching; parents should make kids stick with activities
As a kid he hopped between judo, swimming, soccer, wrestling and taekwondo before bodybuilding stuck as his true love
Practice is immersion of the spirit; the act of lifting has value even without progression
Scheduled days off make you eager to return, while impromptu skipped days breed more laziness
People who blame genetics usually don't really train much, or train unfocused and poorly
He got addicted to training; he still won't miss more than two or three days and finds a gym when traveling
Doing the thing kills anxiety: skipping deadlifts built anxiety until he went back and it vanished
An unbreakable spirit needs an unbreakable body, built by training on a disciplined schedule
Hard work must be balanced with rest
Most manipulators simply lack scruples; protecting yourself is your responsibility
Teach people to take responsibility and see through manipulation rather than babying victims
Once a belief becomes identity it's very hard to convince someone they were fooled
Don't aim for a PhD in bodybuilding; express passion through the body and people will listen because you look the part
